div.head: VI Atr 11
div.ab: K. ⁊ we lærað swyþe geornlice, þæt æghwilc Christen man unriht hæmed georne forbuge ⁊ Christene lage rihtlice healde.
⁊ we lærað swyþe geornlice þæt æghwilc Christen man unriht hæmed georne forbuge ⁊ Christene lage rihtlice healde.
And we lærað swyþe geornlice, þæt æghwilc Christen man unrihthæmed georne forbuge and Christene lage rihtlice healde.
Und wir lehren recht ernstlich, dass jeder christliche Mensch willig gesetzwidrigen Beischlaf meide und die geistlichen Rechtsordnungen gesetzlich halte.
And we teach very earnestly that every Christian man eagerly avoid unlawful intercourse and keep the Christian law rightly.
And we very earnestly enjoin upon every Christian man carefully to avoid illicit unions and duly to observe the laws of the church.
And we very fervently charge each Christian to diligently avoid unlawful intercourse and rightly uphold the divine law.

div.note: AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 166 / 167, October 2026 (was “(*genƏ-and *genu-1,”, now “(*genə- and *genu-¹,”)

his fourth cousin or closer: This phrase has sometimes been translated as “within the fourth knee,” but given the similar Indo-European roots for “kinship” and “knee” (*genə- and *genu-¹, respectively), they may be more accurately translated as “within the fourth degree of kinship” (with thanks to Robert Fulk for pointing this out). In other words, the text rules that a man may not marry anyone to whom he is related as a fourth cousin or closer.
